title: Subscription Management — Big data
description: The k6 big-data run (scripts/bigdata-test.js, resource k6-bigdata): dataset growth per phase, the pipeline into Reporting and how PostgreSQL / PgBouncer / Redis / the services change as the data grows.

panels.title: Dataset growth and phases (k6: seed → renew → cancel + read)
Subscriptions created
panels.description: Seed phase: size of the dataset so far.

panels.title: Renewals accepted
panels.description: Each one is an invoice: outbox → Relay → RabbitMQ saga → Payments → Kafka → Reporting.

panels.title: Reporting invoices (since start)
panels.description: InvoiceIssued facts the Reporting read model holds, counted from the start of the run.

panels.title: Reporting lag (invoices)
panels.description: Invoices the renewal schedule has issued minus the ones Reporting reflects. Overstated when k6 drops iterations.

panels.title: Time to consistency
panels.description: Seconds between the last accepted renewal and Reporting holding all of its invoices.

panels.title: Client req/s by phase
panels.description: Phases are the k6 scenarios: seed, renew, cancel, read, monitor. VUs on the right axis.

panels.title: Random page of the big table (keyset search)
panels.description: POST /subscriptions/search at a random cursor: should stay flat while the table grows (index on start_date, id).

panels.title: Failed requests and dropped iterations by phase
panels.description: Dropped iterations = the load generator could not start requests at the planned rate (not the system's fault).

panels.title: Pipeline to Reporting: API outbox → RabbitMQ → Payments → Kafka → read model
Reporting catches up: scheduled vs reflected invoices
panels.description: The gap between the lines is the latency of the whole chain under load; it closes after the renew phase.

panels.title: Reporting read model since the start
PostgreSQL and PgBouncer as the data grows
Rows per second
panels.description: returned >> fetched means rows are scanned and thrown away: a missing index or a seq scan on the big table.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio · temp files
panels.description: The hit ratio falls once the working set no longer fits shared buffers; temp bytes = sorts/hashes spilling to disk.
